scope: The whole branch against workspace, 9e4e9e274..b8dd4f3f2. An independent reviewer read the diff at 148533531 with issue #1713, rules.md's Planning-records branch rule, deliver-mode.md steps 1-12, Task Merge, Issue Delivery, Sync Epic, Task Delivery and Test Evidence, board.py's row_delivered and progress.py's use of it; it grepped the skill for commit links, --link and the delivered rule, and probed sync.py on fixtures for parsing, idempotency, the two-deliveries refusals, the report line and the delivered rule. b8dd4f3f2 fixes its three blocking findings and finding 5; the session re-read that delta and ran the suites.

AC2: test_sync's commit-link tests (linked once and idempotent, beside a pull request either order, short SHA refused, commit beside an open pull request undelivered) and test_board's row_delivered test. AC3: Task Delivery's commit example and the --link map description; the checker resolves every link.
validation: At b8dd4f3f2: planner suite 1188 tests OK (1 skipped); shared suite 295 tests OK; check_skill_files.py skills/work-planner 65 files, 0 findings; git diff --check clean; pull_request_body.py on the body: no findings.

findings.description: The step-6 Sync Epic body for an engineering-only unit was never saved, so the commit link never reached the epic issue.
Skipping steps 7-10 skipped Task Merge, so an engineering-only unit's criteria, task issue and epic were never settled.
The push bullet preceded the bullets that write and test the files in step 6.
Sync Epic's --link text read as linking the commit for every unit that pushes engineering, while rules.md links it only for a unit changing that branch alone.
